html:
The Chono were canoe nomads of the fjords and islands of southern Chile, between the island of Chiloé and the Taitao Peninsula, an area still called the Chonos Archipelago. They are among the sea nomads of Patagonia.

They lived in their plank canoes, gathering shellfish, fishing and hunting seals and sea lions, and wore cloaks of bark and seal skin. Their language is almost unknown. From the late 1500s Spanish settlers on Chiloé raided them for slaves, and in the 1700s Jesuits of the Society of Jesus moved some to mission islands. Disease and mixing with the Kawésqar to the south and the Huilliche of Chiloé ended them as a separate people by the 1800s.
